hypothesis: On the fastest correct tiled base, computing acceleration directly removes the per-interaction target-mass multiplication and final per-target mass division. Using rsqrtf(distSq) cubed also avoids sqrt and division in each interaction. The reassociation and approximate reciprocal square root may affect numerical results, so this is only a hypothesis until the controller checks correctness and measures it.
notes: Only src/nbody_kernel.cu changes; the selected T1 launch configuration remains block=128, items_per_block=128, shared_memory_bytes=4096. Source tiles, interaction order, self-interaction exclusion, state update order, and exact mass copying are retained. This adapted arithmetic idea has not been compiled or measured here; correctness and performance are for the controller to establish.
transformations: Retain T1's 128-thread, one-target-per-thread mapping and 256-source shared-memory tiles.
Accumulate acceleration directly by cancelling the positive target mass from the force and final division.
Replace sqrt/division-based inverse-distance cubing with rsqrtf(distSq) and two multiplications.
